chapter: Boyhood and the West End camps
title: Bucking against Punch and Rene
summary: He competed with Punch and Rene when bands played side by side at the camps, blowing hard enough to split his lip.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Oh, I bucked against Pant Hook Lane, even Punch. I played against Punch, Rene. They used to come out there and they'd be... You couldn't help it. You'd be playing the dancers and they'd come in and play right next to you.
How did that feel when you were bucking against those guys?

Well, they'd just make you blow your heart out, Dick, that's all. I've seen myself blow so much, split my lip wide open. Just trying to hit them high notes at them, you know. And that's what the whole thing was. They'd just see who could out blow the other fella. And man, that music in those tin roof camps really sound nice. Incidentally, I played a job about five years ago on the 4th of July with Johnny McGee. He played with me and old Bill Wally was with us. We had a five piece combo. Talk about sounding nice, Dick. At Lil Woods. Not Lil Woods, between Lil Woods and the airport. One of those camps.
